name: RetryPolicy
purpose: Describe under which conditions a failed call may be retried, bounded by max attempts, backoff with jitter, a retry budget and an idempotency requirement.
api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Callable, Awaitable, TypeVar

T = TypeVar('T')

class RetryPolicy(Protocol):
    max_attempts: int
    initial_interval_ms: int
    multiplier: float
    max_interval_ms: int
    jitter: float
    budget_ratio: float
    requires_idempotency: bool
    def should_retry(self, attempt: int, exc: BaseException) -> bool: ...
    def next_delay_ms(self, attempt: int) -> int: ...
    async def execute(self, fn: Callable[[], Awaitable[T]]) -> T: ...
invariants: A call MUST NEVER be retried unless it is marked idempotent or the policy has requires_idempotency set to False by an explicit operator decision.
The total retry attempts across a service MUST NEVER exceed budget_ratio of successful traffic in the trailing window.
Backoff intervals SHALL include jitter in the range [0, jitter * base_interval] to prevent synchronized retry storms.
Retries CANNOT be issued when the governing TimeoutBudget.remaining_ms is less than or equal to zero.
A retry policy SHALL classify errors as retryable, non-retryable, or fatal and NEVER retry a non-retryable error.
extension_contract: Adopters subclass or register a RetryClassifier that maps exceptions to retryable or fatal, and bind a BackoffStrategy provider (exponential, exponential_with_jitter, decorrelated_jitter). The retry budget enforcer is sealed and reads from a shared metric source.

sources.source: Google SRE Workbook (Beyer et al., O'Reilly, 2018)
sources.locator: Chapter 22 'Addressing Cascading Failures', section 'Retries' introducing retry amplification and budgets

sources.source: AWS Architecture Blog, 'Exponential Backoff and Jitter' (Marc Brooker, 2015)

why_essential: Ad-hoc retry loops scattered in call sites collide with timeouts and each other, multiplying failing traffic by factors of N per layer; a shared, budget-aware policy is the only place to cap that amplification.
alternatives_considered: Transport-level retry only (HTTP client default): lacks knowledge of idempotency and budget.
Caller-written try/except loops: reinvent classification and NEVER coordinate across callers.
Fire-and-forget retries via queue: shifts the problem and CANNOT enforce deadlines.
